slot.brief: Use the definition of a parabola (distance to focus = distance to directrix) to identify the focus of a given parabola.

stem: The focus of the parabola $(3x+4y)^2=100(4x-3y)$ is

verdicts.working: Set u=(4x−3y)/5 and v=(3x+4y)/5. Then v²=20u, whose focus is (u,v)=(5,0). Transforming back gives (x,y)=(4,−3).

working:
Set $X=\dfrac{3x+4y}{5}$ and $Y=\dfrac{4x-3y}{5}$; these are orthogonal coordinates.
The equation becomes $X^2=20Y$, so $4p=20$ and $p=5$.
The focus in $(X,Y)$ coordinates is $(0,5)$.
Using $x=\dfrac{3X+4Y}{5}$ and $y=\dfrac{4X-3Y}{5}$ gives the focus $(4,-3)$.

Independent check: Set u=(4x−3y)/5 and v=(3x+4y)/5. Then v²=20u, whose focus is (u,v)=(5,0). Transforming back gives (x,y)=(4,−3).
